# T5 — Within-market comparison on switching markets (Task 2.4, methodology D3)

*Generated by `analysis/t5_switchers.py` on 2026-10-09 from release 2026-10-05; regenerate rather than edit. Every number below is read from the T5 tables written in the same run.*

**Status: exploratory.** `docs/analysis_plan.md` (which lists this test as H3) is still a draft with no registration date, so this result was computed before registration.

## Claim

Within the same market × item and month × item, imputed cells' absolute local monthly change is smaller than observed cells' in all four items (every 95% CI, market and two-way, below 0): PPML coefficients on `imputed` range from -0.474 to -0.373 across the four items (imputed/observed ratio of mean |e| 0.623 to 0.689).

Whether this is more than noise removal depends on the survey-noise estimate. Against the A_main benchmark (naive white-noise estimator; the lower of the two reliabilities, so the more demanding test of 'more than noise removed'; it overstates noise under white survey noise but not under stale-quote noise, Table A4) the coefficient is below the benchmark in 1 of 4 items at the point estimate and significantly below (one-sided, Holm, 5%) in 0 of 4. Against A_trim1 (rel with the 1% largest changes trimmed) it is below in 4 of 4 at the point estimate and significantly below in 4 of 4; on the population A_trim1 was estimated on (`matched_trim1`), significantly below in 4 of 4. With the c_-based observed side and its own matched rel, significantly below in 4 of 4 (A_main_c) and 4 of 4 (A_trim1_c).

**The squared-change version needs no Gaussian assumption and gets equal weight.** With outcome e² and benchmark log rel, the coefficient is below the A_main benchmark in 4 of 4 items at the point estimate (significantly in 1) and below A_trim1 in 4 of 4 (significantly in 4). The |e| verdict counts above depend on a Gaussian shape that the data reject (see the 'Gaussian benchmark' caveat), so the two outcomes are reported side by side.

Across the sensitivity specs (below), the count of items significantly below the benchmark ranges A_main: 0–1 of 4 over 5 specs; A_trim1: 4 of 4 over 6 specs.

**These verdicts treat rel as known.** With rel re-estimated on each bootstrap draw (B = 1000), the number of items significantly below the benchmark (bootstrap one-sided p, Holm, 5%) is 0 of 4 for A_main and 0 of 4 for A_trim1; for the item average the share of draws below the benchmark is 0.469 (A_main) and 0.961 (A_trim1). Bootstrap SD of the benchmark itself vs of the coefficient — A_main: benchmark SD exceeds coefficient SD for rice, wheat_flour, oil, lentils (rice 0.396 vs 0.070, wheat_flour 0.428 vs 0.137, oil 0.382 vs 0.140, lentils 0.341 vs 0.119); A_trim1: benchmark SD exceeds coefficient SD for rice, lentils (rice 0.214 vs 0.070, wheat_flour 0.111 vs 0.137, oil 0.113 vs 0.140, lentils 0.229 vs 0.119).

*Reading (inference):* a coefficient below the benchmark means imputed local changes are less dispersed than the true local changes would be once survey noise is removed, i.e. more than noise was removed. The verdict is therefore stated for each noise estimate, not as one answer.

Each draw resamples markets and months (2020-01 on) jointly for the noise sample (Table 1 sample A) and the PPML sample, as Table 1 does. A draw with rel ≤ 0 (estimated noise exceeds total variance) has benchmark −∞ and counts as not below (coef − bench = +∞, so a CI bound can be inf; the SD of coef − bench uses finite draws). p boot = share of draws with coef − bench ≥ 0. The two-way pigeonhole bootstrap is known to be conservative for crossed designs (Owen 2007); bootstrap SD of the coefficient exceeds the analytic SE used in every item (rice 0.070 vs 0.050, wheat_flour 0.137 vs 0.102, oil 0.140 vs 0.117, lentils 0.119 vs 0.093).

## Which cells enter (2020-01 on, four items, latest release)

| cell type | division_market | enters | mixed_change | no_outcome | not_switching |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| II | 1786 | 13890 | 0 | 973 | 4831 |
| IO | 5 | 0 | 992 | 0 | 0 |
| OI | 28 | 0 | 993 | 0 | 0 |
| OO | 149 | 12433 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

Cell types: OO = observed t and t-1; II = imputed t and t-1; OI = imputed t, observed t-1; IO = observed t, imputed t-1; start = no previous month in the panel. Reasons, first that applies: division_market > mixed_change > excluded_by_rule > no_outcome (e undefined: no observed change in that item-month, so the observed-cell month mean is undefined) > not_switching (market × item without both an entering OO and an entering II cell) > enters. Per-item counts: T5_switchers_sample.csv.

Outcome: OO cells use e_obs = log(y_t / y_{t−1}) − μ_t (survey values, both months observed); II cells use e_pub = log(c_t / c_{t−1}) − μ_t (published values, both months imputed); μ_t = mean survey change of all observed cells in that item-month of the latest release (panel column mu_obs; it includes the '… Division' series while they are observed, last observed 2020-07).

## Caveats

- **Gaussian benchmark.** log sqrt(rel) assumes Gaussian e and noise. The shape ratio mean|e| / rms(e) is 0.350–0.595 for observed and 0.367–0.673 for imputed cells (Gaussian 0.798). The PPML coefficient on |e| ≈ log(rms ratio) + log(shape_imp / shape_obs), so different shapes move it away from the benchmark even for a pure noise remover; the shape term log(shape_imp / shape_obs) by item is rice -0.484, wheat_flour 0.333, oil 0.437, lentils 0.529 (column shape_term). The `squared` spec avoids the assumption but weights large changes heavily.
- **Population of rel.** rel comes from observed changes in non-Division markets from 2020-08 (Table 1, sample A); the main sample starts 2020-01 (`from_2020_08` matches the period). The A_trim1 rel describes changes below the 1% trim cut, so applying it to untrimmed |e| mixes populations; `matched_trim1` is the matched comparison (imputed-side 99th-percentile cuts, % units: rice 49.25, wheat_flour 10.87, oil 9.33, lentils 17.06).
- **Noisy μ in thinly observed months.** μ is the mean of the observed changes in the item-month; where few markets are observed it is noisy, and that noise enters every imputed cell's e_pub of that month but not the observed cells' e_obs. Item-months with entering cells whose μ rests on a single observed change: rice 2020-04, rice 2020-05. Share of entering cells in item-months with fewer than 10 observed changes: rice 0.166, wheat_flour 0.118, oil 0.098, lentils 0.123. `mu_min10` drops them; the threshold was chosen after seeing these months.
- **Imputations are the latest release's.** Inference from the release design (history is re-estimated in every release): imputed values in the latest release can draw on survey values from later months, so this compares spells as published now, not real-time nowcasts. The hold-out tables (T3) are the real-time test.
- **Two-way SEs.** CGM variances need not be PSD; 0 of 32 item-level two-way variances were negative (the market-clustered SE is then used).
- **Event windows** are bounded by the adjacent spells; spells are short, so composition changes across event months. `balanced` rows in T5_switchers_event_means.csv keep only events with full windows on both sides. The event-study PPML pools items with item-specific FE.
- **Mixed changes excluded.** The first month of each new spell is a mixed (survey→model or model→survey) change and is excluded from the main sample; `incl_mixed` adds the imputed-after-observed cells.
